environment: Windows 11 Pro x64, MSVC 19.51, GNS 1.6.1 and OpenSSL 3.6.5 via vcpkg 65a2c23, loopback, one process, real time, 1 ms loop
game_exe_sha256: N/A (prototype does not touch the game)
objective: KI-35, reviews #27/#28 (FB-28-01/02): does client-side gating (confirm_binding: the host acks the client's verified binding; the client authenticates only after that ack) improve stall-reconnect recovery, at what cost, and does it stay secure? Owner-authorised behaviour change behind a flag that is off by default.
hypothesis: Predeclared (fade3f7, pushed before any run): O1 P(total > 3 s) on - off with a 95% Newcombe interval; O2 p95/p99 differences with a seeded bootstrap (43, 4000); O3 p50 cost on harsh and latency-only profiles (reported); O4 any first request dropped by the host in arm on without a client gate timeout is a defect. Recommend adoption only if O1 or O2-p95 shows on better on a backend, on worse on none, and no defect.
procedure: confirm_binding implemented (fc5eed3) with 7 security/regression tests on both backends (FB-28-02); a first design gating both sides was caught by a test and replaced by host-acks / client-gates. tools/ki35/reconnect_probe.cpp with arm off|on and profile harsh|latency; tools/ki35/run_ab_probe.py: harsh UDP 4301-4303 and 3 GNS repetitions per arm, arms alternating, 100 cycles; latency-only (80 + U[0,40] ms, no loss) 50 cycles per arm and backend. Three Codex reviews of the tooling before trusting a result (two found evidence-gate defects, fixed with regressions; the third, during the run, approved). Run on a68552d (clean).
expected_result: Arm on removes first-request drops; whether that moves the tail was the question.
observed_result: Complete (16/16 batches, exit 0): 1200 harsh and 200 latency reconnects, 0 timeouts, 0 failures, 0 gate timeouts, 0 unassessable. O4: 0 defects; first-request drops D1 went from 150/300 to 0/300 (UDP) and 76/300 to 0/300 (GNS); ConnectRequests per reconnect 2.04 to 1.35 (UDP) and 1.67 to 1.36 (GNS); session-phase p50 702 to 208 ms (UDP), 223 to 195 ms (GNS). O1 P(total > 3 s): UDP 25/300 off vs 32/300 on, difference 95% [-0.024, +0.071]; GNS 88/300 vs 81/300, [-0.095, +0.049]: no difference shown on either. O2: p95 UDP 3365 vs 3557 ms (diff +192, [-615, +698]), GNS 4492 vs 4775 (+283, [-142, +747]); p99 UDP 4867 vs 4919, GNS 6059 vs 6321: no difference shown. O3 p50: harsh UDP -151 ms [-248, +108], GNS +33 [-139, +165]; latency-only UDP -198 [-302, +180], GNS +185 [+164, +202] (the gate's round trip where the first request was rarely dropped). Homogeneity held (p >= 0.0128). Recommendation by the predeclared rule: DO NOT RECOMMEND.
errors: The experiment ran as predeclared; the hypothesis that removing first-request drops improves the slow tail is not supported: the tail is dominated by DTLS and (on GNS) establishment (EXP-041), which gating does not touch. Gating moves time from the session phase into DTLS (the client waits for the ack). One process, loopback, simulated impairment.
follow_up: Keep confirm_binding off by default (no adoption). KI-35's tail lies in DTLS retransmission and GNS establishment: next, the separate predeclared DTLS-timer and cookie experiments (FB-25-07 / FB-28-04). The 0.04 P(D1) gap (FB-28-03) stays exploratory.
